text:
I need to write a reference letter. I manage a 400-cow dairy farm, and one of our workers, Tomás, is applying to the two-year agricultural technology program at the state technical college.

What I know about him:
- He's worked for us for 3 years, since he was 19.
- He runs the 3 a.m. milking shift on his own, 5 days a week.
- He learned our herd management software and now flags sick cows for the vet. Last winter he caught 9 cases of mastitis early.
- He left for 5 weeks in the middle of last summer when his father got sick in Mexico. He told me 2 days before he left.
- His written English is weaker than his spoken English. He's taking a night class for it.
- He has missed 2 shifts in 3 years, not counting those 5 weeks.

One page, from me as farm manager.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your notes already give the letter its main argument: Tomás runs a shift alone and has learned to read the herd data well enough to catch sickness early. The answers below would make it stronger, or help it handle the weaker points honestly.

1. **Names and addressing.** What are your name, title and farm name, and the farm's town? What is Tomás's surname? What are the college's exact name and program title? Is there a specific person or committee to address, or should I use "Admissions Committee"? I won't make any of these up.

2. **The 5-week absence.** Did you keep his job open, and did he come back when he said he would? How did the farm cover the 3 a.m. shift? Do you want it in the letter at all? I'd lean toward one plain sentence: a family emergency, short notice, he came back and picked up where he left off. Two days' notice reads very differently next to a sick father and a return on schedule. But it's your call, and it depends on what really happened.

3. **Written English.** This is the objection an admissions reader is most likely to have about a technical program with coursework. Do you have anything that answers it? For example: he enters notes or health flags in the software in English, he writes shift logs, he's passed a level of the night class, or how long he's been taking it.

4. **The mastitis cases.** Do you know what catching them early meant in practice: fewer cows lost, less milk dumped, lower treatment costs, or how last winter compared with earlier ones? Has your vet said anything about his flags? Also, what software is it? A named system tells the college he already uses the tools they teach.

5. **What you'll commit to.** Would you rehire him after the program, or keep him on part-time while he studies? If you'd say so, it's the strongest thing a reference from an employer can say. I'll only include it if you say you stand behind it.

6. **Anything else the college will see.** Does the application ask referees to cover anything in particular, like a form, set questions or a word limit? And is there anything else about Tomás the reader might find out that I should handle in the letter?

If you don't know some of these, just say so and I'll write without them.

1. I'm Mike Hollis, farm manager at Hollis Dairy. His name is Tomás Reyes. I don't know the town question matters but I don't have the exact college or program name in front of me beyond what I said. Use "Admissions Committee." It's due February 1 through the college's online portal.

2. Before he left he got his cousin, who used to work for us, to cover his shifts. He came back on the day he said he would. Yes, put it in, one plain sentence like you said.

3. Don't know about the software notes or class level. I don't know how long he's been in the class.

4. The vet said catching them early saved us about $8,000. Don't know the other details or how it compared to past winters. I don't know the software name offhand.

5. I can keep his job open part-time on weekends while he's in the program. I can't pay any of his tuition. I can also take a phone call from the committee, 555-0187.

6. Don't know about a form or word limit. One thing they might see: he failed the written test in a dairy safety course once and passed it the second time.

<final_document>
Dear Admissions Committee,

I am writing to recommend Tomás Reyes for your two-year agricultural technology program. I am the farm manager at Hollis Dairy, a 400-cow operation. Tomás has worked for me for three years, since he was 19. He is one of the most dependable people on my crew, and he already uses the kind of technology your program teaches.

Five days a week, Tomás runs our 3 a.m. milking shift by himself. At that hour there is no one else to check the work. The cows, the equipment and the start of our whole day depend on him getting it right, and he does. In three years he has missed two shifts.

He also learned our herd management software, and he now uses it to flag sick cows for our veterinarian. Last winter he caught nine cases of mastitis early. Our vet estimates that catching them early saved the farm about $8,000. That is the work of someone who understands both the animals and the data, and I think it is exactly the kind of student your program is built for.

Last summer his father became ill in Mexico, and Tomás was away for five weeks. He gave me two days' notice and arranged for his cousin, a former employee of ours, to cover his shifts. He came back on the day he said he would.

His written English is weaker than his spoken English. He once failed the written test in a dairy safety course and passed it on his second try. He is now taking a night class in English while still working the early shift. He became the person on our farm who reads the herd data and spots trouble before anyone else does, and I expect him to work at his writing the same way.

While he is in the program, I will keep a part-time weekend job open for him at Hollis Dairy.

I recommend Tomás without reservation. If the committee would like to talk with me, please call me at 555-0187.

Sincerely,

Mike Hollis
Farm Manager
Hollis Dairy
555-0187
</final_document>

The letter comes to about 350 words, so it fits on one page with room left over.

- **No date:** Add one when you upload it. It's due February 1 through the portal.
- **Tuition:** I didn't mention it. Admissions doesn't decide on funding, so saying you can't pay would only raise a question nobody asked.
- **Check the portal:** It may have a form or set questions for referees instead of a letter upload. If it does, most of this text can be pasted into those fields.
- **Program name:** If you get the exact college and program name, put it in the first sentence. That's the only change you'd need.
